5. The learned Munsif decreed the suit upon finding that plaintiff No. 1 had no bonafide intention to execute the alleged deed and the genuineness of the same was doubtful as the other daughter (defendant No.2) did not come to contest the suit. 

 6. The learned Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Comilla, on appeal, agreed with the findings of the learned Munsif and affirmed the judgment and decree by his order dated 19.4.79. 

 7. Respondents 1 and 2 preferred a revision against the appellate judgment and decree in which the impugned judgment and order have been passed. 

 9. The appellants in their application (8.11.79) for being added as parties in the HighCourt Division stated that plaintiff No.1 after obtaining decree in the trial court transferred out of the suit property .60 decimals of land by two registered sale deeds in their favour in cosideration of Tk. 6000/-, Tk. 3000/- for each kabala, and that the appellants have been in possession of the said land to the knowledge of the defendants. It appears from the impugned judgment that the learned Judge rejected this application on the ground that they were not necessary or proper parties by virtue of their purchase. At the same time it was noticed that Sona Miah (appellant No.1) was already on record on his own petition as one of the heirs and successors of plaintiff No.1 and thus he was fully represented in the revision case. Be it mentioned that plaintiff No.1 who was opposite party No.1 in the said revision case died during the pendency of the said case and was substituted by his heirs, the daughters (who were already on record) and appellant No.1.
